14 A trailer of weight 30 kN is attached to a cab at X, as shown in the diagram.
cab
trailer
X
30 kN
10 m
10 m
What is the upward force exerted at X by the cab on the trailer?
A
3 kN
B
15 kN
C
30 kN
D
60 kN

hints: Notice the trailer has two upward supports: the rear wheels and the cab at X, with the $30 \text{ kN}$ weight acting $10 \text{ m}$ from each.
For balance the resultant force is zero and the resultant moment about any point is zero, so take moments about the rear axle to eliminate its unknown force.
Set clockwise moment from the $30 \text{ kN}$ weight equal to the anticlockwise moment from the force at X acting $20 \text{ m}$ from the rear axle.
walkthrough: Identify the trailer as a beam in equilibrium supported at the rear wheels and at X, with weight $30 \text{ kN}$ acting downwards midway between them.
From the diagram the weight is $10 \text{ m}$ forward of the rear wheels and X is $20 \text{ m}$ forward of the rear wheels.
Use the principle of moments: for equilibrium, sum of moments about any point is zero. Take moments about the rear wheels so the rear normal has zero moment.
Let $F_X$ be the upward force at X. Then $F_X \times 20 \text{ m} - 30 \text{ kN} \times 10 \text{ m} = 0$.
Rearrange and calculate: $F_X = (30 \times 10)/20 = 15 \text{ kN}$. Units are $\text{kN}$ and vertical forces then sum to $30 \text{ kN}$ as required.

A.explanation: Too small. $3 \text{ kN}$ would not give zero resultant moment about the rear wheels for a $30 \text{ kN}$ weight $10 \text{ m}$ away.

B.explanation: Taking moments about the rear wheels gives $F_X \times 20 \text{ m} = 30 \text{ kN} \times 10 \text{ m}$, so $F_X = 15 \text{ kN}$ upward.

C.explanation: The cab does not support the full $30 \text{ kN}$ because the trailer rear wheels also provide an upward force sharing the weight.

D.explanation: Greater than the total weight. In vertical equilibrium the two upward supports must sum to $30 \text{ kN}$, so $60 \text{ kN}$ is impossible.
